messages:
deploybot: [ALERT] Canary check failed for embed-service in us-west2: consistent 12% 5xx on new image redwood/embed:v1.3.0-nightly. Rollout paused. Need expedited decision: pin to v1.2.9 or allow rollback.

maya: Noted. Is this customer-facing or internal test traffic?

jordan: Customer-facing. A subset of requests hit quant kernel and threw decode errors. Repro on staging.

maya: My recommendation — pin to redwood/embed:v1.2.9-stable and scale down v1.3.0. Ops, can you supervise the pin and monitor for 15m?

ops_oncall: I can take it. If we pin, monitor keys: error_rate, p99 latency, and CPU steal. I'll escalate if any metric >5% above baseline.

jordan: Running pin command:
```
/releasebot pin --service embed-service --image redwood/embed:v1.2.9-stable --reason "canary regressions v1.3.0" --urgency emergency --owner jordan
```

releasebot: Received. Verifying image sig and deploy policy... OK. Applying pin and rebalancing traffic now. ETA 40s.

deploybot: Traffic reroute complete. All user traffic back on redwood/embed:v1.2.9-stable. v1.3.0 canary scaled to zero.

maya: I'll draft a short blurb for release notes + internal slack: "Pinned to v1.2.9 due to canary regressions in v1.3.0. Investigations assigned to jordan, will follow up with postmortem."

ops_oncall: Monitoring started. error_rate returned to baseline (~0.5%). Holding watch for 15m. If any spike, I'll trigger rollback to v1.2.8 and page SRE.

jordan: Logged issue: quant kernel flag mismatch between build and runtime. Starting bisect.

ops_oncall: +17m stable, no anomalies. Marking expedite window closed.

maya: Thanks everyone — marking thread resolved and adding postmortem owners.
